ATR(14) = 103.03 index points, 14 sessions ending 16 Jun 2026, computed on cash-session bars (16:30-23:00 broker = 09:30-16:00 ET). R = 45.06 pts = 0.44 x ATR(14): inside the 0.3-3.0 band and at or below 1.00, so no wide-stop flag; 2R = 90.11 is below 3 x ATR = 309.09, so no 'TP2 ambitious' flag. Confluences at the stop: daily S1 7,503.60 less a 0.25 x ATR buffer, with the 16 Jun session low 7,518.20 just above it. INDICATIVE-LEVEL QUALIFIER: the stop is buffered off a daily pivot whose prior-period high/low inputs the report flags as single-source indicative; the level is carried with that qualifier. rationale: REFERENCE CLOSE: 7,522.90, the settled close of 16 Jun 2026 - the last completed cash session strictly before the report date D = 17 Jun 2026 - read from the slice on the cash-session basis (16:30-23:00 broker). The report's own 7,548.60 is +25.70 against this and fails the 3-pt close tolerance, so every level here is re-derived from the slice, not from the report's price table. BASIS: all figures on cash-session bars, the basis the report's asset (the S&P 500 cash index) trades on and the basis the QA reference uses. ATR14 = 103.03 index points, mean true range over the 14 cash sessions ending 16 Jun 2026 (TR = max(H-L, |H-PrevC|, |L-PrevC|)); the report's asserted ~150 is 46% high and is discarded. Full-day-bar ATR14 on the same window is 117.14, quoted only because the linter recomputes on that basis. DIRECTION: the report's §21a conviction score is +0.30 LONG, above the 0.25 threshold, so Trade 1 is not suppressed on the conviction gate. ENTRY: M5 §5.1 sets Trade 1 as a market or just-fillable order at the daily-open anchor, and §5.0 fixes the fill level at the D-1 reference close, so entry = 7,522.90 exactly. The report's buy limit 7,558 with a conditional market fallback is a dual-mode entry sitting 35.10 above the reference close - the wrong side for a long limit - and is rebuilt, not annotated. ANCHOR: 09:00 broker. The report states 07:00 UK in its §2 session note and again in its §20 log, where it records the anchor as 'overridden to 07:00 UK per run instruction'. M5 §5.0 and §9a row 4 forbid re-selecting a fixed anchor at run time, and a run-time instruction is not authority to do so; the standing anchor therefore governs. No level moves either way, because with the broker clock at UTC+3 and the UK on BST, 07:00 UK converts to exactly 09:00 broker - the report's own stated time and the standing anchor are the same instant. STOP: M5 §4c takes the tighter of the 5-day swing extreme or the nearest support, with a 0.25 x ATR14 = 25.76 buffer beyond it, capped at 3.5 x ATR14 = 360.60. Candidates below the reference close, tightest first: the 16 Jun session low 7,518.20 (nearest support in the 5-day structure) less the buffer = 7,492.44, giving R = 30.46 = 0.296 x ATR - below the 0.30 x ATR floor of 30.91, which M5 §9a row 6 requires be rebuilt rather than warned; next, daily S1 7,503.60 less the buffer = 7,477.84, giving R = 45.06 = 0.437 x ATR, inside the 0.3-3.0 band and well inside the 3.5 x ATR cap; last, the 5-day swing low 7,260.00 (11 Jun 2026) less the buffer = 7,234.24, giving R = 288.66 = 2.80 x ATR, compliant but far wider and it would carry the wide-stop flag. The tightest compliant anchor is daily S1, so stop = 7,477.84 and R = 45.06 points. PIVOTS: daily floor pivots from the D-1 session itself (16 Jun 2026 cash H 7,571.40 / L 7,518.20 / C 7,522.90) per M3 Step 8, P = (H+L+C)/3 = 7,537.50, R1 = 2P-L = 7,556.80, S1 = 2P-H = 7,503.60, R2 = P+(H-L) = 7,590.70, S2 = P-(H-L) = 7,484.30, R3 = H+2(P-L) = 7,610.00, S3 = L-2(H-P) = 7,450.40. Identity check R2-P = P-S2 = H-L = 53.20 holds. The report's daily pivots are 19.30-24.60 points high because they are built on its own uncorroborated 16 Jun H/L/C. TARGETS: M5 §5.1 gives TP1 = entry + 1R = 7,522.90 + 45.06 = 7,567.96 (+45.06 pts) and TP2 = entry + 2R = 7,613.01 (+90.11 pts). TP1 sits 45.06 points from entry, inside the 2.5 x ATR = 257.57 reachability bound. TP3 is the runner: session-close time stop, or the 3 x ATR14 price cap at 7,522.90 + 309.09 = 7,831.99 (+309.09 pts), whichever comes first; it is printed as a number rather than left as prose, and it is beyond TP2. The report's extracted tp3 of 7,800 appears nowhere in the report text and is discarded. LADDER: 7,477.84 < 7,522.90 < 7,567.96 < 7,613.01 < 7,831.99, ordered for a long. SUPPRESSION GATES TESTED: conviction +0.30 vs threshold 0.25 - does not fire; ATR14 present, positive - does not fire. NO SWING FIB LEVEL IS USED ON THIS CARD, so no fib percentages apply here.

strategy: Trade 2 - Pivot, TRANSITION branch (breakout side only) - SUPPRESSED
entry_mode_text: n/a - suppressed. No entry, stop, R or target ladder is carried.
management_text: SUPPRESSED - every accessible pivot tier carries the single-source-indicative corroboration flag. No entry, stop, R or target ladder is carried, per the suppression rule that a suppressed card is a row and not a card.
rationale: REFERENCE CLOSE: 7,522.90, the settled cash close of 16 Jun 2026, the last completed session strictly before D = 17 Jun 2026. ATR14 = 103.03 index points on the 14 cash sessions ending 16 Jun 2026. BRANCH: the report resolves the regime to TRANSITION in its §9 - 'the dual gate for a clean RANGE or TREND is not satisfied' - and that single label governs the Trade 2 branch and the Trade 3 fork alike. Under TRANSITION, M5 §5.2c permits the breakout side only: a counter-side limit is suppressed, not re-labelled. The report's shipped card - a mean-reversion buy limit at daily S1 - is a RANGE construction under a TRANSITION label and is discarded rather than repaired. HAD THE CARD BEEN ELIGIBLE, the TRANSITION branch mirrors the §5.2b breakout geometry on the upside with the slice pivots: entry = P + 0.10 x (R1 - P) = 7,537.50 + 0.10 x 19.30 = 7,539.43 as a buy stop, 16.53 above the reference close and therefore on the correct side; the §5.2b primary stop P - 0.8 x (P - S1) = 7,510.38 gives R = 29.05 = 0.282 x ATR, under the 0.30 x ATR floor of 30.91, so it would have had to be rebuilt onto the S1 - 0.25 x ATR anchor at 7,477.84 for R = 61.59 = 0.60 x ATR, with targets R1 7,556.80 / R1.5 7,573.75 / R2 7,590.70. These numbers are recorded for audit only. SUPPRESSION TRIGGER THAT FIRES: all accessible pivot tiers carry the SINGLE-SOURCE-INDICATIVE flag. The report's §19 states it in terms - every intraday open/high/low field is reconstructed and flagged indicative, and 'all pivot prior-period H/L inputs inherit the single-source-indicative flag, which §21 reads when assessing Trade 2' - which is a statement that every pivot tier, daily, weekly and monthly, is indicative. M5 §5.2a makes that test symmetric: where the report states anywhere that every pivot tier is indicative, the card is suppressed, and if a card is produced instead, the report must name which tier is corroborated and by which second source. No such second source exists inside the permitted inputs. The one candidate the report itself cites - the Investing.com 16 Jun range 7,516.75-7,577.92 - sits 1.45 and 6.52 points from the slice high and low, far outside the plus or minus 0.10-point equity-index corroboration tolerance, so it does not corroborate the prior-period high and low and the pivots cannot be promoted. The report's own basis for shipping the card anyway - logged in its §20 as 'not fully suppressed, since a corroborated prior close anchors the pivot midpoint' - does not clear the gate, because the pivot P is a function of the prior high, low AND close, and the report's §19 rests that relaxation on a run instruction; the suppression triggers are explicitly non-overridable by any run-time direction, and stating the flag and shipping the card regardless is the exact failure the rule exists to prevent. OTHER GATES TESTED: regime branch resolved to TRANSITION - correct branch selected, does not itself suppress; ATR14 present and positive - does not fire. Trade 1 is not suppressed by this trigger: the indicative flag propagates there as a qualifier on a stop that is merely buffered off daily S1, whereas Trade 2's entry, stop and every target are pivot levels.

rationale: REFERENCE CLOSE: 7,522.90, the settled cash close of 16 Jun 2026, the last completed session strictly before D = 17 Jun 2026. ATR14 = 103.03 index points on the 14 cash sessions ending 16 Jun 2026, cash-session bars. FORK: the regime label is TRANSITION, as the report resolves it in its §9, and the Trade 3 mapping is fixed with no discretion - TRANSITION forks to 3C, the momentum-breakout. The report's card is headed 3A, the momentum-pullback fork that belongs to a TREND label, and is then built as a breakout stop entry over the 16 Jun high, so it is neither the fork the label selects nor the geometry its own heading claims. A variant may not be substituted because its levels look more tradeable; where the selected variant fails its own eligibility test the outcome is the suppressed row. RANGE DEFINITION: the 25-session boundaries from the slice are swing high 7,624.60, printed 2 Jun 2026, and swing low 7,243.10, printed 9 Jun 2026, giving a width of 381.50 points. ELIGIBILITY TEST THAT FAILS: a confirmed break requires a daily close beyond the boundary by at least 0.25 x ATR14 = 25.76 points. Upside that is a close at or above 7,624.60 + 25.76 = 7,650.36; downside a close at or below 7,243.10 - 25.76 = 7,217.34. The 16 Jun reference close of 7,522.90 is 127.46 points below the upside level and 305.56 above the downside one, and no session in the window closed beyond either boundary - the 25-session high itself was set two weeks earlier and has not been reclaimed. Without the confirming close the trade is not eligible, and the suppression trigger for no confirmed break in a TRANSITION regime fires. The direction recorded is the side the breakout would take if it were confirmed - upside, on the report's read of a five-session recovery pressing the range top with the failed retests at the upper boundary - but no order, level or ladder is carried. HAD THE BREAK BEEN CONFIRMED, the geometry would have been stop = range low + 0.40 x width = 7,243.10 + 152.60 = 7,395.70, TP1 = entry + 1.0 x width = entry + 381.50, TP2 = entry + 1.5 x width = entry + 572.25, recorded for audit only. NO FIB RETRACEMENT APPLIES: the 57.5% / 38.2% / 0% / 100% ladder belongs to the 3A fork, which this label does not select. For the record the qualifying swing on the slice would have been 7,260.00 on 11 Jun 2026 up to 7,583.40 on 15 Jun 2026, magnitude 323.40, which clears the 2 x ATR14 = 206.06 threshold - but 3A is not the fork here and its levels are not emitted.
